cards.title: What 'the Cloud' actually is — no sky involved!
cards.takeaway: Cloud storage simply means saving your files on secure internet servers (like Google Drive) instead of only on one phone or laptop.
cards.body:
Think of keeping cash under your mattress vs. keeping money in a bank account:
- **Local storage only:** If your phone falls in water or your laptop is stolen, your only copy is gone.
- **Cloud storage (Google Drive):** Your files live safely online linked to your Google account. Log in from **any** phone or laptop and your files are waiting for you!

cards.title: The 3 folder rules: Shallow, Numbered, and Predictable
cards.takeaway: Keep folders shallow (2–3 levels max), numbered (`01_Admin`, `02_Sales`), and named consistently so anyone finds any file in 5 seconds.
cards.body:
A messy Google Drive wastes hours every month. Follow three golden rules:
1. **Shallow:** Avoid burying files 8 folders deep — 2 to 3 levels is plenty.
2. **Numbered:** Prefix main folders (`01_Clients`, `02_Invoices`, `03_Marketing`) so they stay in your chosen order instead of jumping alphabetically.
3. **Predictable file names:** Write `2026-09_Adaeze_Invoice_04.pdf` instead of `final_new2.pdf`!

check.prompt: Why do we keep Google Drive folders 'shallow, numbered, and predictable'?

choices.text: Because Google charges extra money for unnumbered folders
So folders stay in a logical order and you can find any file in seconds instead of digging through chaos
Because Drive deletes files whose names have spaces
So nobody else can ever view your files

check.hint: Imagine searching urgently for a September invoice while a client waits on the phone.
check.explanation: Exactly! Shallow, numbered folders and consistent file names stop files from getting lost in deep, confusing subfolders.

cards.title: Sharing safely: Viewer vs. Commenter vs. Editor
cards.takeaway: Viewer can only read, Commenter can leave suggestions without changing your words, and Editor can change or delete content.
cards.body:
When you share a file in Google Drive, choose the **least power needed**:
- **Viewer:** Can read/download only (great for sending a finished price list or invoice to a client).
- **Commenter:** Can highlight and leave margin notes, **without** editing your actual text (great for a boss or supervisor reviewing a draft).
- **Editor:** Full power to rewrite or delete (only for trusted teammates building the file with you).

cards.title: The 'Anyone with the link' WhatsApp trap
cards.takeaway: Never set an 'Anyone with the link = Editor' link and drop it in a public WhatsApp group — strangers can forward it and wipe your file!
cards.body:
**Watch out for this real-world mistake:**
If you set a file to **Anyone with the link** (especially as *Editor*) and post it in a busy WhatsApp group:
- Anyone can forward that link outside the group.
- Strangers can view private customer data or accidentally delete your work!

**Fix:** Keep sensitive files **Restricted** and share directly with specific people's email addresses (as *Viewer* or *Commenter*).

check.prompt: Which Google Drive permission lets your supervisor leave notes on your draft WITHOUT changing your text?
check.hint: Viewer can only read; Editor can rewrite everything; which one sits safely in the middle?
check.explanation: Spot on! Commenter lets someone add feedback notes without altering your actual document.

cards.title: Finding any file fast with Drive Search
cards.takeaway: Combine file type and keywords — like `type:pdf invoice` or the search filter chips — to pull up exact files in two seconds.
cards.body:
Even with hundreds of files, Google Drive's search bar at the top finds things instantly:
- Type **`type:pdf invoice`** (or click the **PDFs** + **Date modified** filter chips) to find all PDF invoices from a specific month like September 2026.
- You can also navigate straight into your numbered `02_Invoices/2026-09` folder!

cards.title: Deleted a file by mistake? You have 30 days in Trash!
cards.takeaway: Google Drive keeps deleted files in Trash (Bin) for 30 days — open Trash, right-click the file, and click Restore.
cards.body:
Accidentally deleted an important file? Breathe easy:
1. Open **Trash** (or **Bin**) on the left menu of Google Drive.
2. Deleted items stay there for **30 days** before permanent removal.
3. Right-click your file and click **Restore** — it jumps right back to its original folder!

check.prompt: How long does Google Drive keep a deleted file in the Trash before deleting it forever, and how do you bring it back?

choices.text: 30 days; open Trash, right-click the file, and choose Restore
It cannot be recovered once deleted

check.hint: Think of one calendar month inside the Trash / Bin tab.
check.explanation: Correct! Drive holds deleted files in Trash for 30 days, and right-click → Restore puts them right back.
